title: News-family Clanks: a live editorial intake/review surface must be the default landing view
requirement: A news/lead-based Clank MUST expose a primary editorial intake/review surface (a queue or feed of current, actionable leads/stories awaiting a decision), and that surface MUST be the default view an operator lands on — reachable without navigating away from the entry point, whether that is a dedicated route or the single page a Clank happens to have.
rationale: Independently present in all three surveyed news-family Clanks, and in each case it is specifically the default/landing view, not merely present somewhere: chinese-tech-wire's Newsroom is served at both '/' and '/newsroom' (the same handler); korean-tech-wire's single page opens with 'Latest Leads' as its first section; semiconductor-intelligence's default-active tab (of 12) is explicitly 'stories'/'Editorial Inbox'. This adds something Pass 1's QC-queue standards did not establish: not just that a queue exists, but that it is the thing an operator sees first.
forbidden: A news-family Clank whose default landing view is a stats page, a source-health page, or anything other than the live intake/review surface
acceptance: The default route/view (whatever an operator reaches with no navigation) is, or immediately contains, the current actionable leads/stories awaiting review
This can be satisfied by a dedicated route being the default, or by a single-page app placing it as the first/primary section

evidence.summary: '/' and '/newsroom' map to the same handler — the lead review queue is the default landing view.
'Latest Leads' is the first section of the single page served at '/'.
The 'stories' ('Editorial Inbox') tab is explicitly the default-active tab among 12.

notes: Pass 2 candidate. 3/3 of surveyed news-family Clanks independently satisfy this, which is the full news-family sample from this pass.
